[1;38;5;78mTHE DIRECTION: one
disease, two
audiences — the
console and its
instrument both stop
asserting what they
did not measure[0m

This wave has one
sentence and it
points in both
directions at once.
A system that could
not determine
something must say
so. It must not
substitute a
plausible guess, a
default, or the
negative branch of a
two-way test it was
unable to run.

Pointed at the
INSTRUMENT, that
sentence resolves
the lead's binary by
refusing it. Option
(a) alone leaves the
predicate lying in
every other shallow
environment — a
container, a fork
PR, an agent's `--
depth 1`, any future
job. Option (b)
alone leaves
standing the fact
the lead correctly
identified as bigger
than the test: that
every seal run under
this workflow is
structurally unable
to evaluate clause
(b). The answer that
pays both is the
DISCRIMINATION:
teach the git legs
to tell rc 1 (“not
an ancestor”, an
honest answer about
the product) from rc
128 / missing object
/ shallow repository
(“I could not look”,
an honest answer
about the
environment). Once
the predicate can
tell those apart,
(b) becomes the
correct shape for
the control — it
asserts the floor it
is actually about —
and (a) becomes a
verified environment
declaration rather
than a workaround,
because a regression
back to depth-1
would then produce
an honest INFRA-
FAULT the job can
assert on.

Pointed at the
PERSON, the same
sentence is already
sitting in the
ledger as open rows.
A refused connection
is reported as “A
network step timed
out. Retry usually
fixes this.” — the
console did not
classify the
failure, so it
guessed, and the
guess carries
ADVICE. A person
switches on
“Deployment failed”
alerts across email
and every chat
channel, and the
event has zero
producers anywhere
in the repository —
the console tells
them they are
subscribed to
something that
cannot arrive. These
are not clipping
bugs. They are the
epic's founding
vision, in its
purest form, and
they are the wave's
person bodies.
